# Imported data structure

\`ImportWeather()\` returns a long-format data frame with four columns. Each
date is repeated once for each weather variable, which makes it straightforward
to filter, group, summarise and plot individual measurements.

| Output column | Type | Meaning |
|:--|:--|:--|
| \`Date\` | Date | Calendar date of the daily observation. |
| \`DOY\` | Integer/numeric | Day of year supplied by the workbook (1–365, or 1–366 in leap years). |
| \`variable\` | Character | Name of the weather variable. |
| \`value\` | Numeric | Daily value for that variable, in the units described below. |

# Weather variables

The \`variable\` column contains the following labels. Units are taken from the
workbook field names and plotting labels; consult the station's instrument
metadata for the precise measurement convention and calibration.

| Variable label | Unit / scale | Interpretation |
|:--|:--|:--|
| \`Temperature deg C Min\` | °C | Daily minimum air temperature. |
| \`Temperature deg C Max\` | °C | Daily maximum air temperature. |
| \`Air temp Mean\` | °C | Daily mean air temperature. |
| \`Temp diff deg C\` | °C | Daily temperature difference as supplied by the workbook. |
| \`Rainfall mm\` | mm | Daily rainfall total. |
| \`Soil 15cm deg C\` | °C | Soil temperature at 15 cm depth. |
| \`Soil 45cm deg C\` | °C | Soil temperature at 45 cm depth. |
| \`Average Wind speed Km/h\` | km/h | Daily average wind speed. |
| \`RH (%)\` | % | Relative humidity. |
| \`Leaf wetness (U)\` | U (source scale) | Leaf-wetness measurement; the workbook label does not define a physical unit. |
| \`Lite totals daily (W/m2)\` | W/m² (source label) | Daily light/solar-radiation total as labelled in the workbook. Confirm whether the station reports an accumulated energy or an average irradiance before converting or comparing it. |

# Derived plotting variable

\`PlotMonthlyGrid(variable = "temperature_range")\` is a convenience view, not
an additional imported measurement. It combines \`Temperature deg C Min\` and
\`Temperature deg C Max\` for the same date and displays the range.

# Missing values and coverage

Missing measurements remain \`NA\` in the imported long data. Summary functions
exclude missing values from calculations; a group with no observed values
remains \`NA\`. The importer filters to the requested date range, but does not
create rows for dates absent from the workbook. Check date coverage before
interpreting monthly totals or long-term summaries.

# Example

\`\`\`{r, eval = FALSE}
weather <- ImportWeather(
  file = "crossnacreevy.xlsx",
  start_date = "2020-01-01",
  end_date = "2024-12-31"
)

dplyr::filter(weather, variable == "Rainfall mm")
\`\`\`

# Source and interpretation

This dictionary documents the names and units exposed by the package. It is
not a substitute for the station's formal metadata, instrument manuals or
quality-control flags. The package does not infer missing observations,
perform sensor calibration, or independently validate the scientific
meaning of workbook fields.
